posts.title: How to pack a storage unit so you can still reach everything
posts.excerpt: The mistake is packing it like a removal van. Here is the layout that leaves an aisle and keeps the things you need at the front.
posts.content:
Most people pack a storage unit the way they would pack a removal van: biggest things in first, everything wedged together, doors closed on a solid wall of stuff. It works for the van, because the van gets unloaded all at once. A storage unit does not.

Leave an aisle. Always.

The single biggest improvement is an aisle down the middle — or along one side in a narrow unit. It costs you about a fifth of the floor area, and it means you can reach the back without unloading the front.

That fifth is already built into the size calculator's recommendations, which is why it sometimes suggests a size bigger than you expected.

If you cannot reach it without unloading half the unit, you do not really have it stored — you have it buried.

Heavy at the bottom, often-needed at the front

  • Books, tools and anything dense go in small boxes, on the floor.
  • Things you will want back soon — seasonal clothes, paperwork, the good pans — go nearest the door.
  • Label two sides of every box, not just the top. Once boxes are stacked, the top is the one side you cannot see.

Stand sofas on their end

An upright sofa takes about a third of the floor space. Wrap it in a breathable cover rather than plastic sheeting, which traps moisture against the fabric.

Use the height

Every StoreBox unit is at least 2.4 m tall. Boxes of the same size stack safely to about 2.2 m, so buying one size of box — rather than collecting whatever the supermarket had — is worth more than it sounds.

Keep a gap of a few centimetres from the walls for air to circulate, and put a pallet or a couple of planks under anything that should not touch concrete.

Keep a list on your phone

Photograph each box before you seal it, and number them. When you are looking for the kettle in three months' time, you will know it is in box 14, left-hand stack, second from the bottom.

posts.title: About
posts.content:
Home / About

About

In 2014 the options were a damp garage or a warehouse with a four-page contract. So we built the thing we wanted to rent.

Our story

Simple storage, done properly.

Our founders were between flats with a houseful of furniture and nowhere to put it. The places they found wanted a deposit, a twelve-month contract and a viewing appointment three days away.

So in 2014 we opened our first facility in Amsterdam Noord with one rule: it should be as easy to rent a storage unit as it is to book a hotel room. No deposit, no minimum term, and a price you can see before you call.

Twelve years and three facilities later, that is still the rule.

What we stand for

Three promises we have never broken.

01

The price you see is the price you pay

No admin fee, no deposit, and no increase in your first twelve months. If a competitor is cheaper for the same size, tell us.

02

Your things, your key

Only you can open your unit. Staff cannot get in without you, and we never cut a lock without a court order.

03

Leave whenever you like

Two weeks' notice, unused days refunded. We would rather you came back than felt trapped.

Since 2014

From one corridor to three facilities.

Grown entirely by word of mouth, which is why we still answer the phone ourselves.

2014

Amsterdam Noord opens

84 units on a single floor of a former print works.

2017

Second floor, climate control

Noord grows to 318 units, all heated and ventilated.

2020

Amsterdam Zuidoost

Our first drive-up site: every door at ground level.

2023

Haarlem Oudeweg

Built around business storage, with pallet delivery and racking.

2026

Reserve online, move in today

The whole process moves online, from quote to PIN.
